source.publication: 2025 Expanded Instructions (IA 1040) and the 2025 IA 1040 Iowa Individual Income Tax Return
source.section: IA 1040 form PDF p.1 Step 3 lines a, b, d; form PDF p.2 lines 1c, 2-5, 7, 8, 11, 12; Instructions PDF p.8 Step 3; PDF p.9-10 lines 2-4; PDF p.12 line 5 ('Iowa now has a flat tax rate of 3.8%'); PDF p.18 line 12

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (you) 45,000.00 = 45,000.00. Federal taxable income = 45,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 for 65 or older = 27,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). IA 1040 filing status 1 (single). Step 3 line a personal credits 1 x 40.00 = 40.00; line b 1 x 20.00 = 20.00 (65 or older on or before January 1, 2026; nobody blind); line c no dependents; line d and line 8 = 60.00. Line 1c federal AGI 45,000.00; line 2 federal taxable income 27,250.00. Schedule 1: no additions or subtractions. Schedule 1 line 21 net modifications = 0.00; line 3 = 0.00. Line 4 Iowa taxable income = 27,250.00 + (0.00) = 27,250.00. Line 5 tax = 3.8% x 27,250.00 = 1,035.50; line 7 = 1,035.50. Line 11 total credits 60.00; line 12 balance = 1,035.50 - 60.00 = 975.50. State income tax 975.50 (no line 13-17 credits; line 19 school district or EMS surtax is local, not computed). The form allows whole-dollar rounding; expected keeps the cents. Low-income exemption test (PDF p.10-11): line 4 27,250.00 + federal deduction 17,750.00 = 45,000.00, against 24,000.00: not exempt. Single filers' tax reduction (PDF p.18): its worksheet 41-146 is not in the sources, so it is not applied. Born 1961-01-01: 65 on January 1, 2026, which the booklet's 'on or before January 1, 2026' includes (PDF p.8), and the age input is 65 by the tax rule, so the 65 credit applies. The form and this figure agree; the projection's January 1 approximation does not bite on this input.
accepted_approximations: School district and county EMS surtaxes (a percentage of the tax, form line 19) are local and out of scope (issue #1).
